summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Natural selection operates through differential reproductive success. Three modes: (1) Stabilizing selection narrows the curve around the mean phenotype (e.g. human birth weight); (2) Directional selection shifts the population mean toward one extreme (e.g. industrial melanism, antibiotic resistance); (3) Disruptive selection favors both extremes over the mean, generating a bimodal distribution.

conceptBreakdown.content:
### 6.1 Three Modes of Natural Selection
1. **Stabilizing (Centripetal) Selection**:
   - Favors the intermediate mean phenotype and eliminates phenotypic extremes.
   - *Result*: Peak gets higher and narrower, reducing phenotypic variance.
   - *Example*: **Human birth weight**—infants weighing $3\text{--}4\text{ kg}$ exhibit maximum survival; babies significantly lighter ($<2\text{ kg}$) or heavier ($>5\text{ kg}$) suffer high mortality.
2. **Directional (Progressive) Selection**:
   - Favors individuals at one extreme of the phenotypic range.
   - *Result*: Peak shifts continuously in one direction.
   - *Examples*: **Industrial Melanism** in *Biston betularia*, evolution of **Antibiotic Resistance** in bacteria, and **Pesticide / DDT Resistance** in mosquitoes.
3. **Disruptive (Diversifying) Selection**:
   - Favors individuals at both phenotypic extremes simultaneously while selecting against the intermediate mean.
   - *Result*: Splits a unimodal curve into two distinct peaks (bimodal distribution), potentially initiating sympatric speciation.

### 6.2 Industrial Melanism in Peppered Moths (*Biston betularia*)
- **Pre-Industrial England (Before 1850s)**: Lichen-covered pale tree barks camouflaged light-colored moths (*typica*). Dark melanic mutants (*carbonaria*) were easily spotted and predated by birds $\longrightarrow$ **White moths dominated**.
- **Post-Industrial England (After 1850s)**: Industrial soot blackened tree bark and killed sensitive lichens. Dark melanic moths became camouflaged against soot; light moths were heavily predated $\longrightarrow$ **Dark moths dominated via Directional Natural Selection**.
- *Key Principle*: Natural selection acted on **pre-existing mutations**; pollution did not induce the melanic allele.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Anthropogenic Selection and Superbugs
conceptBreakdown.title: Anthropogenic Selection and Superbugs
conceptBreakdown.content: Excessive clinical use of antibiotics exerts intense directional anthropogenic selection, selecting for rare pre-existing plasmid-borne multi-drug resistance genes (e.g., MRSA, NDM-1 metallo-beta-lactamase).

conceptBreakdown.heading: Balancing Selection (Heterozygote Advantage)
conceptBreakdown.title: Balancing Selection (Heterozygote Advantage)
conceptBreakdown.content: Sickle-cell trait (HbA/HbS) in malaria-endemic regions represents Balancing Selection, where heterozygotes have higher Darwinian fitness than both normal (HbA/HbA - malaria vulnerable) and diseased (HbS/HbS - lethal anemia) homozygotes.
